During the hair model making process, to create a better shape, there may be some relatively complex mesh structures. If the board clips through, it will be unstable, so we need to add a layer of downy mesh. OK, now after finishing the 3D model, we will discuss the downy mesh material.  

Because normal hair, like the hair on my side, after importing into CLO, looks like this. You cannot see a layer of wrapping mesh outside. But in the modeling stage, there is such a layer of mesh. To make it invisible in CLO, we need to adjust its material settings.  

First, go to the material slot, add a new material, and assign it to our downy mesh. Then rename it accordingly.  

Then for the downy mesh material, set its base color. Some software call it color map, some call it default map, but they are the same – used to assign color textures.  

Click on the base color, select image texture, then click open image. I prepared a fully transparent image beforehand, made in Photoshop without any pixels, just a gray and white checkerboard pattern. Click open image.  

This way, the base color texture is a fully transparent image. In CLO, it will appear fully transparent. This is how the downy mesh material is handled.  

After finishing this, select the hair object, then export the file. Please pay attention to export format: FBX. When exporting, be careful with the path, because if the path is not handled well, texture loss may occur.  

Here, I choose a copy method and check "selected objects" because I only selected the hair. Otherwise, the entire avatar will be exported. Then, object type: only export mesh. Do not export cameras, lights, or other elements. Then click export FBX. The FBX is exported.  

Check if you have any questions about making hair models. You can model hair yourself in software, or purchase many model resources on online shopping platforms. After purchase, adjust slightly according to your virtual model’s head shape, and it can be used directly.  

OK.  

Didn’t download Blender? Don’t know if it’s easy to install? Blender is very easy to install. It is open-source software and free to use. Just search on Baidu for Blender’s official website and download it.  

We are using Blender now.  

After exporting this FBX, next we open CLO.  

Now I delete the current hair. After exporting FBX, open CLO, then open the exported FBX in CLO to confirm its position and size are correct.  

This is mainly to avoid issues during import/export such as axis orientation or unit problems that cause size or position errors.  

Once confirmed no problems, we can make custom hair.  

Select the virtual model, customize hair and shoes.  

Here, please note a very important point. For example, if your hair is bound to Feifei, open Feifei. If you are binding to Lanmo, open Lanmo. The hair binding will be attached to the currently opened virtual model.  

We select hair here, then load the exported FBX. Select the FBX just exported, then open the thumbnail. Thumbnails are pre-made small images; you can also create them by snapshotting in FBX import process to confirm position.  

After loading, click generate. A popup window appears; save the file and name it as hair. Click save. It will take some time to calculate.  

Let’s see what you guys say.  

About molding (pinching) – currently pinching is not supported in CLO. You can do pinching in Dash or other 3D software using sculpting tools.  

After finishing, there will be a prompt box. I will close it here. The generated hair is this one. The file format is ZACS. Drag this file in, and you will see the hair is completed.  

Next, let’s see how to make the hair downy mesh. Some may wonder how to do it. It’s not very difficult. First, delete the original downy mesh. In object mode, create a new UV sphere.  

Adjust the mesh count higher slightly, no problem. Adjust its size, this is a bit small. OK. Then move it onto the model's head.  

Open its mesh and check if it completely covers the hair model. OK, fully covered.  

Switch display mode. Then in Blender, use the modifier tool called Shrinkwrap. Select Shrinkwrap, then select the target as our hair. It will wrap the UV sphere mesh around the hair model by nearest point.  

You can adjust the offset so it doesn’t have too large deformation. Switch display mode to check.  

Note: don’t make the offset too big, e.g., 5 cm. Although it covers the hair, it will increase the overall hair volume. The downy mesh also participates in collision calculations.  

If you later make clothes with a hood on top of this hair, an oversized downy mesh will push the hood outward, making the shape look bad, not tight to the hair.  

So be careful not to make it too big. A little slight clipping is OK; we will fix it later with other tools.  

After applying the Shrinkwrap modifier, apply it to complete.  

Next, enter sculpt mode to do detailed adjustments. As time is limited, I haven’t finished the whole thing, since it takes a lot of time.  

For those unfamiliar with other 3D software basics, you can search for tutorials and follow along. It’s quite simple. I’m not a master either, just an enthusiast, but I can do it.  

After finishing, merge this downy mesh sphere and hair together. Then apply the downy mesh material to it and export.  

Downy mesh acts like a protective film, wrapping the hair to prevent clipping between the board and hair which causes simulation instability.  

This is the hair making process.  

Next, let’s talk about making shoes. Then I will continue going back to Blender.  

Open a Blender file prepared before. Shoes are done similarly to hair. Put the shoe on the model's foot.  

Also add a downy mesh like before, wrapping the entire shoe. This is useful for relatively long styles, e.g., skirts or long pants, to prevent board instability with shoes.  

Add an extra protective film layer.  

Where to download this software? Blender can be downloaded directly from its official website. It’s free software.  

I want to do short hair. Here’s a small tip. Sorry, I just missed an important point.  

When customizing hair for this virtual model, please try to do short hair. Short hair or tied back, like a bun, is better. Don’t make overly long hair.  

Because the hair causes conflicts. If your hair is over the shoulder, it becomes inconvenient to make clothes. You might only do lower body or chest or one-piece shoulder clothing. Otherwise, the hair will conflict with the board, making collars and such impossible.  

If you want a really beautiful character with long hair, then make the clothes first, finalize the pose, then transfer everything to another 3D software to make long hair. This involves long hair, model pose, and some clothing positioning. After adjustment, transfer back to CLO to showcase.  

This is the process for long hair.  

Now back to shoes. Besides adding a downy mesh as before, there is also an important point for high heels.  

For high heel shoes, the heel must be a separate material. That is, the entire heel part should have a heel material applied. This material should be positioned at the bottom of all materials.  

This is a software recognition rule. So when making custom high heels, pay close attention to this. Otherwise, it will fail.  

Maybe some of you want to change shoe colors in CLO. You can separate materials for different parts, like the diamond part and the bottom.  

If you want to make such shoes, set their materials separately in your software. For example, diamond surface uses one material, the bottom another.  

After separating different materials, in CLO you can assign different colors and material settings to various parts.  

After completing the shoe, export it.  

When exporting shoes, please split the mesh into two objects: left shoe and right shoe.  

The left shoe must be named "Shoes Left" (case insensitive but exact spelling). The right shoe named "Shoes Right".  

After naming, select both shoes, then export FBX. Export only selected objects, only mesh. This is the same as hair export process. Then export.  

Let’s see questions.  

Can tall boots be made? Yes, same as shoes. If your tall boots have high heels, heel mesh must have heel material applied and placed at the bottom of all materials. Objects named "Shoes Left" and "Shoes Right". All shoes follow this naming rule. Boots can be done similarly.  

Can material settings be done in Brand? Brand's material settings and CLO's are not interoperable because their base material data is different. However, textures can be shared. For example, CLO texture maps like base color can be shared with Brand.  

Where to download Brand software? Search on Baidu for Brand official website, then go to download page.  

After exporting shoes, import FBX into CLO and check position and size. If no problems, you can customize it.  

Delete the shoe in CLO, then select virtual model pose for high heels, as shoe is high heels.  

Select virtual model, customize hair and shoes, choose shoes, select high heels, load the shoe FBX, add thumbnail, click generate, save.  

A normal shoe is done. You don’t have to worry about whether you will use it like this later. The first time, we did it this way because the foot is positioned correctly. If you open a virtual model with default shoes, then put high heels shoes in, it will display normally without foot lifted.  

This is shoe production.  

Next, let's talk about default components. Put a costume on to conveniently discuss default zipper. Open it in front view.  

Then I will talk about default zipper later. There are many things you can do with default zipper.  

Go to Blender. Open a zipper OBJ file made in advance.  

First, a description. It’s a zipper in CLO. There are four types of zippers. We have several types: zipper with zipper on top and bottom, total four types. I will focus on explaining this zipper with zipper on top and bottom.  

Making zipper is easier than hair or shoes because as long as you place it correctly and size is correct, no problem.  

First, place zipper and slider together on the Z axis. In Blender, Z axis is vertical; other software might differ, but it must be vertical. Place in middle position.  

It has a pull head (slider handle), this is the pull ring position, the ground grid is below it, then zipper. Adjust position well.  

In front view, the X axis (red line) corresponds to the pull head position aligning with zipper teeth position.  

When modeling, make sure the object is placed at the middle bite position on X axis.  

After finishing, very important point: set the origin point (pivot) of the object to the world coordinate center. For example, for the pull, set origin point to the object center.  

This ensures that when selecting the pull, the pivot is centered properly, avoiding position problems in CLO.  

After setting origin, select pull, export together. Export OBJ format, select OBJ group, selected objects only. Name the files, e.g., separate slider and puller.  

Then import into CLO, select pull and puller OBJ, preview, adjust position as needed. Use refresh if you want to reset to original position. Confirm to complete preset.  

Next, create pull chain. There will be a broadcast online after a week. Our old users know we upload broadcasts after a week.  

The pull chain is ready to install. After installation, click to open puller. See the puller and puller we just set up. Click to switch. This is puller and puller selection.  

Next is individual export. First, export the slider. Its position is the same as the pull and zipper together. Place at the middle of Z axis, center point aligned. In top view, the X axis matches the zipper teeth position.  

Export OBJ for slider.  

In CLO, you can customize zipper by clicking plus sign and selecting zipper. Select slider, click OBJ file, open slider. Preview shows slider position. If not correct, adjust position along Z axis (front-back direction in CLO).  

Adjust slider to proper position, then confirm. This creates zipper preset. Confirm. CLO automatically uses the created slider. This exits the combined state of slider and puller. This is slider creation.  

About graphics cards: yes, they are expensive now because many people are mining.  

Next, let's talk about zipper teeth (pull tab). Export of pull tab is separate.  

Because pull tab and slider were exported together, there may be some offset. We need to adjust position.  

In top view, move the center point of pull tab to coordinate origin, keep same height. Set origin point. Select pull tab, add guide, export OBJ.  

In CLO, select pull tab OBJ, confirm, create preview.  

Someone asked about making a helmet. It’s possible but tricky. CLO is made of soft plates, not easy to make smooth, round shapes like helmets. Better to make helmets in other software.  

Next, talk about upper zipper part. It should be placed at the bottom of the floor grid, top of model parallel to floor grid. Align origin point properly.  

Put matching zipper parts together and export as two parts: left and right edges. Select both and export together.  

In CLO, add custom zipper, select corresponding OBJ files for left and right parts.  

Be careful to assign left and right correctly.  

Open OBJ files, confirm. Adjust shapes as needed.  

Next, export open zipper mouth parts separately, the zipper and lock are separated. Export OBJ for zipper mouth and lock separately.  

When making zipper mouth, only bottom part of lock below ground and middle position between left and right mouth is used.  

In preview, zipper teeth align correctly.  

Add these parts in CLO zipper settings. Confirm to complete.  

Last is closed zipper, simplest, just one OBJ placed below grid with bite point at X axis center. Export OBJ, add to CLO, preview, confirm. Complete zipper preset.  

Summary: although many operations are done, the key is to set positions correctly for each part, then export. No problem if done right.  

Next, about custom buttons. Some noticed new versions have more complex custom button features.  

After clicking, a window appears with many options and explanations.  

This update was made because previous custom buttons caused resizing issues. For example, changing size could cause unwanted resizing. So sometimes two OBJ buttons are needed.  

You can add multiple OBJs (two, three, or four) to a custom button.  

Open a new Brand file. There is a button with two OBJs: one blue, one green. These are different sizes, one smaller, one bigger.  

They are not equal in size. Back sewn OBJs are same size. Using custom button function can suddenly relax the whole button, which some users may not want.  

So pre-make two size buttons, create guides for each separately.  

Select large button, add OBJ guide, name "big". Export. Then select small button, add OBJ guide, export.  

Remember to check "selected objects only" to avoid exporting entire environment.  

The button should face up.  

We also have two locks here, facing up. The requirement is the same as before. The origin point must be at the coordinate center.  

In front view, the whole button must be above the grid. If part is below grid, conflicts will occur during simulation, causing instability.  

So the whole OBJ must be above the grid.  

Next, add guides for big and small buttons, export OBJ, assign guides, save.  

In the folder, you can see two OBJ files for the two sizes.  

In CLO, add shortcut, then add lock shutter, select big lock OBJ, set size data for your reference, add new size, load small lock OBJ, name accordingly, confirm to complete lock preset.  

You can now add the customized button in the button tool, set materials, colors, etc.  

This concludes today’s live broadcast content.  

If you have questions, ask in comments, I will answer.  

I will end the live broadcast in 5 minutes. If you want to know more about any content, you can request it for the next live stream.  

I’m happy if everyone learns something.  

Let’s check questions.  

Regarding graphics card configurations, check official website for requirements.  

When is the next live stream? Probably in a month, October 15th.  

Can I do the same for food? What do you mean by "your food"?  

To save the video on your phone, how to convert it to MP4?  

Is your video a spiral video made by CLO or a regular one?  

If CLO does not support the video, you can convert it to MP4.  

If you are comfortable with Deep Vision, you can convert it to MP4.  

If you want to save the original video as MP4, choose MP4 format.  

C4D can do it as well.  

Closed walk video can be saved as MP4 format.  

How to set the qipao button?  

For qipao buttons, you should use plate buttons. These buttons are more suitable for making simple buttons.  

For plate buttons, it is better to make secondary buttons, as long as it’s in OBJ format.  

Live show: we had a previous live show. You can watch it; it is a complete tutorial from zero to finish.  

Sometimes it uses FBX format. When to use FBX? For custom hair and shoes, FBX is required. For custom zipper, buckle, OBJ is used.  

How to sew this pocket zipper?  

This side is actually a fake pocket zipper. It just has a hole dug here.  

You can use the zipper tool to add it here.  

If you wonder about seams at both ends, just pull a bit when modeling. You will see a gap here.  

You can use the sewing tool in the 3D window to sew the zipper and panel together.  

Any other questions?  

Why does hair need FBX? Hair and shoes need FBX format because they require a downy mesh.  

Any other questions?  

If none, today’s live broadcast ends here.  

Thank you all for your attention.  

Earrings won’t fit on ears?  

If you want to make earrings, here’s a quick explanation:  

Just create a circle, make it smaller.  

For earrings, mostly you just need to place them in the correct position.  

If you want earrings to move with the model, one way is to make them like hair format.  

Of course, not suitable for long earrings. For small earrings, when building hair model, customize hair and place it at the ear position.  

When imported, it will be at ear position and can follow the model on the runway.  

How to make necklace fit around the neck?  

Just make the file and simulate it on the neck.  

If it is a complicated necklace, and you want to know how to wear earrings and necklaces on the model or have them walk on the runway, and you are interested, we can do a special live tutorial later about accessories and color matching.  

OK, I originally just wanted to make a simple earring. Put it on the ear like making clothes. Don’t simulate it, just place it and adjust pivot position.  

If the ring is thick, make it thinner. I just set a random value.  

Later during simulation, freeze the whole thing and move it.  

OK, today’s live broadcast ends here.  

Thanks everyone for your support.  

See you next time, bye-bye.  

Thank you all for watching.

chunks.title: [CLO Master Express Lesson 18] Custom Hairstyles & Shoes Live! Come and give your model a makeover~
chunks.content: ## Overview of Custom Hairstyles, Shoes, and Zippers in CLO This section introduces techniques for creating custom hairstyles, shoes, and zippers using CLO and complementary 3D software such as Blender. It covers workflow essentials like model preparation, export formats (FBX for hair and shoes, OBJ for zippers and buckles), unit consistency, mesh orientation, and material settings to ensure compatibility and quality in CLO. --- ## Creating Custom Hairstyles in CLO and Blender This section explains the step-by-step process of making custom hair for virtual models using CLO and Blender, focusing on mesh preparation, downy mesh creation to prevent simulation clipping, material settings, and export/import best practices. ### Model Preparation and Export from CLO - Open the virtual model in CLO (male or female as needed). - Remove default hair and shoes from the model. - Export the virtual model with hair/shoes removed as FBX. - When exporting, ensure: - The "Include Virtual Model" option is checked to export the avatar properly. - File paths and usernames use English with underscores; avoid Chinese characters. ### Importing and Editing in Blender - Set Blender’s unit system to millimeters (mm) to match CLO's centimeters (cm) units and avoid scaling issues. - Import the FBX virtual model into Blender. - Add custom hair meshes onto the virtual model. - Hair meshes often have a "film" or protective layer called the **downy mesh** — a thin outer mesh to prevent clipping between hair and body or clothing. - Verify mesh face orientation: - Front faces (blue) must point outward. - Back faces (red) should be corrected if inward-facing. ### Creating and Applying the Downy Mesh - The downy mesh wraps around the hair to stabilize simulation and prevent clipping. - To create it: - Delete the original downy mesh if present. - Create a new UV sphere in Blender sized to cover the hair completely. - Use the **Shrinkwrap modifier** to conform the sphere mesh onto the hair surface. - Adjust offset carefully; too large offsets increase hair volume and may cause unwanted collisions with clothing. - Apply the modifier and enter sculpt mode for detailed adjustments. - Set the downy mesh material to fully transparent in CLO by assigning a transparent base color texture (e.g., a Photoshop-created transparent image). ### Exporting and Importing Custom Hair Back to CLO - Export the hair and downy mesh as FBX. - Use "Selected Objects Only" and export only mesh objects to avoid extra elements like cameras or lights. - In CLO, delete the original hair and import the custom hair FBX. - Confirm correct position and size to avoid axis or scaling mismatches. - Load the hair FBX and generate a hair asset; save as a ZACS file. - Note: Pinching or sculpting hair within CLO is not supported; use external 3D sculpting tools like Dash. ### Tips for Hair Modeling - Prefer short hair or tied-back styles for easier clothing simulation.
chunks.content_description: Come and learn various methods of creating and importing custom attachments together with Xiao C and Teacher Samantha! Give your model a makeover~

chunks.content: - Use "Selected Objects Only" and export only mesh objects to avoid extra elements like cameras or lights. - In CLO, delete the original hair and import the custom hair FBX. - Confirm correct position and size to avoid axis or scaling mismatches. - Load the hair FBX and generate a hair asset; save as a ZACS file. - Note: Pinching or sculpting hair within CLO is not supported; use external 3D sculpting tools like Dash. ### Tips for Hair Modeling - Prefer short hair or tied-back styles for easier clothing simulation. - Long hair causes conflicts with clothing and simulation; for long hairstyles: - Finalize clothing and model poses first. - Create and adjust hair in external software. - Import completed hair back to CLO for presentation. - Hair and shoes must use FBX format due to downy mesh requirements. --- ## Creating Custom Shoes in CLO and Blender This section details the process for making custom shoes, including flat and high-heeled types, downy mesh application, material separation, and export/import procedures. ### Shoe Model Preparation - Open the virtual model and remove shoes. - Export flat shoe FBX with the virtual model included. - Adjust foot posture for high heels by rotating heel upward in CLO. - Export high heel shoe FBX similarly. ### Editing in Blender - Import shoe FBX files. - Add custom shoe mesh on the foot. - Add a downy mesh layer around the shoe to prevent clipping and simulation instability, especially important for long garments like skirts or pants. - Downy mesh creation and material assignment are similar to those for hair. ### Material Setup for High Heels - The heel part must be assigned a **separate heel material**. - This heel material should be placed at the bottom of the material stack in the 3D software. - This is a CLO software requirement to correctly recognize and simulate high heel shoes. ### Material Separation for Shoe Parts - Different parts of the shoe (e.g., diamond decorations, sole) can be assigned separate materials. - This allows color and texture customization within CLO. ### Exporting Shoes - Split shoe mesh into two objects: "Shoes Left" and "Shoes Right". - Naming is case-insensitive but must be exact. - Export both shoes as FBX, selecting only mesh and selected objects. - Import into CLO, check position and size, then generate shoe assets. - Use appropriate virtual model poses (e.g., high heel pose for high heel shoes). ### Additional Notes - Tall boots follow the same rules as shoes in naming, material assignment, and export. - Brand software material settings differ from CLO's base materials but textures like base color maps can be shared. --- ## Creating Custom Zippers and Buckles with OBJ Format This section covers making custom zippers and buckles using OBJ files, focusing on correct positioning, origin setting, and part separation for CLO compatibility. ### Zipper Types and Placement - CLO supports four zipper types, including zippers with sliders on both top and bottom.

chunks.content: ### Additional Notes - Tall boots follow the same rules as shoes in naming, material assignment, and export. - Brand software material settings differ from CLO's base materials but textures like base color maps can be shared. --- ## Creating Custom Zippers and Buckles with OBJ Format This section covers making custom zippers and buckles using OBJ files, focusing on correct positioning, origin setting, and part separation for CLO compatibility. ### Zipper Types and Placement - CLO supports four zipper types, including zippers with sliders on both top and bottom. - Place zipper and slider aligned on the Z axis (vertical in Blender). - Align pull head (slider handle) and zipper teeth along the X axis in front view. - Set the origin point (pivot) of each object to the world coordinate center to avoid positional errors in CLO. ### Exporting Zipper Components - Export slider and puller separately in OBJ format. - Use "selected objects only" and export as OBJ group. - Import into CLO, adjust positions, preview, and confirm. ### Pull Chain and Pull Tab - Pull chain can be installed after zipper parts are preset. - Pull tab (puller handle) is exported and positioned separately. - Adjust center point to coordinate origin before export. - Import pull tab OBJ into CLO, preview, and confirm. ### Upper and Lower Zipper Parts - Upper zipper parts are aligned parallel to the floor grid. - Export left and right edges as separate OBJ files. - Import and assign left and right parts correctly in CLO. ### Open and Closed Zippers - Open zipper mouth and lock parts are exported separately. - Closed zipper is simplest, one OBJ placed below grid with bite point centered on the X axis. - Import into CLO and confirm zipper presets accordingly. ### Summary - Correct placement, pivot origin, and file naming are crucial. - markdown_content: ## Overview of Custom Hairstyles, Shoes, and Zippers in CLO This section introduces techniques for creating custom hairstyles, shoes, and zippers using CLO and complementary 3D software such as Blender. It covers workflow essentials like model preparation, export formats (FBX for hair and shoes, OBJ for zippers and buckles), unit consistency, mesh orientation, and material settings to ensure compatibility and quality in CLO. --- ## Creating Custom Hairstyles in CLO and Blender This section explains the step-by-step process of making custom hair for virtual models using CLO and Blender, focusing on mesh preparation, downy mesh creation to prevent simulation clipping, material settings, and export/import best practices. ### Model Preparation and Export from CLO - Open the virtual model in CLO (male or female as needed). - Remove default hair and shoes from the model. - Export the virtual model with hair/shoes removed as FBX. - When exporting, ensure: - The "Include Virtual Model" option is checked to export the avatar properly. - File paths and usernames use English with underscores; avoid Chinese characters. ### Importing and Editing in Blender - Set Blender’s unit system to millimeters (mm) to match CLO's centimeters (cm) units and avoid scaling issues. - Import the FBX virtual model into Blender. - Add custom hair meshes onto the virtual model. - Hair meshes often have a "film" or protective layer called the **downy mesh** — a thin outer mesh to prevent clipping between hair and body or clothing. - Verify mesh face orientation: - Front faces (blue) must point outward. - Back faces (red) should be corrected if inward-facing. ### Creating and Applying the Downy Mesh - The downy mesh wraps around the hair to stabilize simulation and prevent clipping. - To create it: - Delete the original downy mesh if present. - Create a new UV sphere in Blender sized to cover the hair completely. - Use the **Shrinkwrap modifier** to conform the sphere mesh onto the hair surface. - Adjust offset carefully; too large offsets increase hair volume and may cause unwanted collisions with clothing. - Apply the modifier and enter sculpt mode for detailed adjustments. - Set the downy mesh material to fully transparent in CLO by assigning a transparent base color texture (e.g., a Photoshop-created transparent image). ### Exporting and Importing Custom Hair Back to CLO - Export the hair and downy mesh as FBX. - Use "Selected Objects Only" and export only mesh objects to avoid extra elements like cameras or lights. - In CLO, delete the original hair and import the custom hair FBX. - Confirm correct position and size to avoid axis or scaling mismatches. - Load the hair FBX and generate a hair asset; save as a ZACS file. - Note: Pinching or sculpting hair within CLO is not supported; use external 3D sculpting tools like Dash. ### Tips for Hair Modeling - Prefer short hair or tied-back styles for easier clothing simulation. - Long hair causes conflicts with clothing and simulation; for long hairstyles: - Finalize clothing and model poses first. - Create and adjust hair in external software. - Import completed hair back to CLO for presentation. - Hair and shoes must use FBX format due to downy mesh requirements. --- ## Creating Custom Shoes in CLO and Blender This section details the process for making custom shoes, including flat and high-heeled types, downy mesh application, material separation, and export/import procedures. ### Shoe Model Preparation - Open the virtual model and remove shoes. - Export flat shoe FBX with the virtual model included. - Adjust foot posture for high heels by rotating heel upward in CLO. - Export high heel shoe FBX similarly. ### Editing in Blender - Import shoe FBX files. - Add custom shoe mesh on the foot. - Add a downy mesh layer around the shoe to prevent clipping and simulation instability, especially important for long garments like skirts or pants. - Downy mesh creation and material assignment are similar to those for hair. ### Material Setup for High Heels - The heel part must be assigned a **separate heel material**. - This heel material should be placed at the bottom of the material stack in the 3D software. - This is a CLO software requirement to correctly recognize and simulate high heel shoes. ### Material Separation for Shoe Parts - Different parts of the shoe (e.g., diamond decorations, sole) can be assigned separate materials. - This allows color and texture customization within CLO. ### Exporting Shoes - Split shoe mesh into two objects: "Shoes Left" and "Shoes Right". - Naming is case-insensitive but must be exact. - Export both shoes as FBX, selecting only mesh and selected objects. - Import into CLO, check position and size, then generate shoe assets. - Use appropriate virtual model poses (e.g., high heel pose for high heel shoes). ### Additional Notes - Tall boots follow the same rules as shoes in naming, material assignment, and export. - Brand software material settings differ from CLO's base materials but textures like base color maps can be shared. --- ## Creating Custom Zippers and Buckles with OBJ Format This section covers making custom zippers and buckles using OBJ files, focusing on correct positioning, origin setting, and part separation for CLO compatibility. ### Zipper Types and Placement - CLO supports four zipper types, including zippers with sliders on both top and bottom. - Place zipper and slider aligned on the Z axis (vertical in Blender). - Align pull head (slider handle) and zipper teeth along the X axis in front view. - Set the origin point (pivot) of each object to the world coordinate center to avoid positional errors in CLO. ### Exporting Zipper Components - Export slider and puller separately in OBJ format. - Use "selected objects only" and export as OBJ group. - Import into CLO, adjust positions, preview, and confirm. ### Pull Chain and Pull Tab - Pull chain can be installed after zipper parts are preset. - Pull tab (puller handle) is exported and positioned separately. - Adjust center point to coordinate origin before export. - Import pull tab OBJ into CLO, preview, and confirm. ### Upper and Lower Zipper Parts - Upper zipper parts are aligned parallel to the floor grid. - Export left and right edges as separate OBJ files. - Import and assign left and right parts correctly in CLO. ### Open and Closed Zippers - Open zipper mouth and lock parts are exported separately. - Closed zipper is simplest, one OBJ placed below grid with bite point centered on the X axis. - Import into CLO and confirm zipper presets accordingly. ### Summary - Correct placement, pivot origin, and file naming are crucial. - Properly exporting zipper components ensures seamless CLO integration. --- ## Custom Buttons in CLO: Advanced Features and Export Workflow This section explains the new custom button features in CLO, including support for multiple OBJ files per button for size variation, guide usage, and export/import procedures. ### Multiple OBJ Support for Buttons - New CLO versions support buttons composed of two, three, or four OBJ files. - This addresses previous issues with button resizing causing unwanted deformation. - For example, one button could have a large and a small OBJ to represent different states. ### Preparing Button OBJs - In 3D software (e.g., Brand), prepare button OBJs in required sizes. - Add OBJ guides in Brand, naming them clearly (e.g., "big", "small"). - Export selected objects only to avoid unwanted elements. - Ensure the button faces upward and is placed entirely above the grid to avoid simulation conflicts. ### Setting Origin Points - Set origin points at the coordinate center for all button parts. - This ensures proper pivot behavior in CLO. ### Importing and Setting Up Buttons in CLO - Add custom button preset. - Import large and small button OBJs separately. - Assign size data and names accordingly. - Confirm to finalize the button preset. - Customize button materials and colors within CLO. --- ## Additional Tips and FAQs ### Software Recommendations and Downloads - Blender and Brand are recommended 3D software for hair, shoe, and zipper editing. - Blender is open-source, free, and easy to install from its official website. - Brand software can be found via Baidu and downloaded from the official site. ### File Format Usage - Use FBX format for custom hair and shoes (due to downy mesh requirements). - Use OBJ format for zippers and buckles. ### Graphics Card Requirements - Current graphics cards are expensive due to mining demands. - Check official CLO website for GPU requirements. ### Accessory Modeling - Earrings can be created as small circles positioned on ears. - For earrings to move with the model, treat them like hair objects. - Necklaces can be simulated on the neck; detailed accessories may require specialized tutorials. ### Simulation and Compatibility Notes - CLO does not currently support hair pinching or sculpting; use external sculpting software. - Long hair is best created after finalizing clothes and poses in external software before importing back into CLO. - Custom buttons and zippers require accurate pivot and grid placement to avoid simulation instability. ### Sewing Pocket Zippers - Fake pocket zippers can be created by making a hole and sewing the zipper onto the panel using CLO's sewing tools. ### Video and Media Format Support - CLO videos can be converted to MP4 using software like Deep Vision or C4D. -
